text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The Islamist-led government to collect tolls from drivers using motorways between provinces as it seeks ways of raising state revenues.
- Foreign Minister Ciller repeats a warning to Iran not to give support to Turkey's rebel Kurds during her visit to Washington.
- The government's 1997 forecasts anticipate a larger than ever budget deficit.
- Istanbul Chamber of Commerce protests at a monthly meeting against European Union plans to freeze financial aid for Turkey under a customs union deal which went into effect in January.

- Cairo delays a reply to Islamist prime minister Erbakan's proposal to visit Egypt. Egyptian President Mubarak's visit to Ankara was marred by disagreement over a trip by Moslem Brotherhood representatives to Turkey.
- Amnesty International is preparing to pressurize Turkey over human rights' violations.
- The heaviest burden to the car manufacturing sector is high import duties.
- Tension in prisons escalates after a prison riot in the eastern city of Diyarbakir claimed 10 lives.
- Fire-fighting services are beset by problems because of the failure to modernise.
